bands.label: Strong
bands.blurb: Solid contracts, transparent operations, and an easy start.

providers.name: Tomorrow.io
providers.description: Tomorrow.io is a Boston-based weather intelligence platform combining a global proprietary numerical weather model, a constellation of microsatellite weather radars, and a developer-facing v4 REST API. The platform exposes 60+ hyperlocal data layers — core weather, air quality, pollen, solar, soil, fire, flood, lightning, maritime, aviation, road — together with map tiles, severe-weather event detection, routable forecast queries, climate normals, historical archive access, customer-defined locations, named insights, and threshold-based webhook alerts. Used by airlines, on-demand logistics platforms, agriculture, energy, and the US Air Force, Tomorrow.io's API is designed for ETA-aware route planning, geofenced alerting, agentic workflows, and large-scale operational decisioning under weather risk.

bands.label: Developing
bands.blurb: Real signal across most facets with visible, nameable gaps.

providers.name: ArcNautical
providers.description: ArcNautical provides vessel sanctions and ownership screening APIs that allow users to check any vessel against OFAC, EU, UN sanctions and ownership chains. The service offers free, no‑key endpoint access for basic checks and detailed risk scoring for voyages, supporting compliance, insurance and financing decisions. It includes a public API with OpenAPI spec, pricing information, blog updates, and security documentation.

providers.name: Starlink
providers.description: Starlink is the low-Earth-orbit satellite internet constellation operated by SpaceX from Hawthorne, California, delivering broadband and non-terrestrial connectivity to residential, business, maritime, aviation, and government customers in the United States and roughly a hundred other markets. In the telecom value chain Starlink is an access-network operator that sells connectivity directly to end customers and wholesales capacity to airlines, shipping lines, and mobile network operators, rather than a CPaaS aggregator or a GSMA-affiliated mobile network operator. Its API posture is unusually open for an access provider and unusually narrow in scope. The Starlink Public API V2 is fully documented in public at starlink.readme.io, its OpenAPI 3.0.4 description is downloadable anonymously from starlink.com with no login, and SpaceX publishes an official gRPC protobuf for the local device API on GitHub. But the API is operational rather than developer-product, covering account, service line, user terminal, router, billing, and telemetry management, and credentials are gated behind an enterprise or business Starlink account whose admin must mint a V2 service account. No CAMARA implementation, no GSMA Open Gateway participation, and no TM Forum Open API conformance was found anywhere in Starlink's published material.

providers.name: Nortech
providers.description: Nortech AI is an industrial IoT and operational-data infrastructure company (Bergen, Norway and Lisbon, Portugal) serving the maritime market and other asset-heavy industries. Its edge-plus-cloud platform extracts high-frequency data directly from industrial machinery, equipment and control systems — across vendors, protocols and equipment age — and structures it into trustworthy, contextualized signals for data-driven decision-making. The Nortech Cloud API exposes a Metadata API (workspaces, assets, divisions, units, signals), a Signal Data API (historical, live and import) and a Deriver API for computed virtual signals, plus an MQTT live-data stream.

providers.name: Sofar Ocean
providers.description: Sofar Ocean operates one of the world's largest privately owned networks of real-time ocean weather sensors. Its Spotter buoys and Smart Mooring subsurface sensors stream wave, wind, sea-surface temperature, barometric pressure, and acoustic data via cellular and satellite telemetry, and the Wayfinder platform turns that data into maritime voyage optimization. The Sofar API (Spotter & Smart Mooring plus the Operational Wave Spectra forecast) gives developers token-authenticated access to device telemetry, historical and geospatial data queries, subsurface sensor readings, NetCDF wave-spectra forecasts, and outbound data-forwarding webhooks.

providers.name: DNV
providers.description: DNV is a global classification, certification, and assurance provider for the maritime, energy, and industrial sectors. The API portfolio includes the Class Status API for vessel classification data, the Veracity industry data platform, and the public Vessel Register, supporting fleet management, regulatory compliance, and operational analytics workflows.

providers.name: SERTICA
providers.description: SERTICA is a maritime fleet and ship management system from RINA (originally built by Logimatic in Denmark, first code written in 1989), used to run planned maintenance, procurement, HSQE, crewing, performance, logbooks and vessel reporting across a fleet. It is deployed as a per-customer site rather than a shared multi-tenant service, and it publishes a genuinely large machine-readable contract: the SERTICA Web API is an OpenAPI 3.0.4 document with 2,743 paths, 3,340 operations and 1,104 schemas, served publicly at https://docs.sertica.com/api/swagger/v1/swagger.json and browsable in a live Swagger UI. It is a REST/JSON API authenticated with a 24-hour JWT obtained by posting a SERTICA user login to /Auth, with authorization expressed as per-user SERTICA user rights rather than OAuth scopes. Beyond CRUD it carries the statutory maritime surface - MARPOL Oil, Garbage and Ballast Water electronic record books with signing and printout operations, SFI-coded components, ISM management-system documents, and PunchOut/ShipServ procurement integration.

providers.name: Portbase
providers.description: Portbase is the Port Community System (PCS) organisation of the Port of Rotterdam Authority and the Port of Amsterdam, digitally connecting the Dutch port community - terminals, shipping companies, transporters, forwarders and government - so that goods and data flows through the Dutch ports and connected chains run efficiently, sustainably and securely. It offers web services and system interfaces (APIs, AS2, sFTP, SMTP and webhooks) for services such as Cargo Controller Import/Export, notifications and cargo declarations, documented in its support centre.

providers.name: Xweather
providers.description: Xweather, a Vaisala company, provides weather data APIs delivering science-backed, hyper-local weather intelligence for operational applications. The Xweather Weather API exposes current conditions, forecasts, severe weather alerts, lightning data, air quality, observations, wildfire information, tropical cyclone tracks, and maritime weather through a single REST API. Authentication uses a client_id and client_secret passed as query parameters or HTTP headers.

providers.name: VesselFinder
providers.description: VesselFinder is a maritime intelligence company operating a global AIS vessel-tracking network (terrestrial AIS plus satellite AIS) and offering ship positions, voyage history, vessel particulars, port-call events, sea-distance routing, and ocean-container track-and-trace through its developer APIs. The platform pairs a credit-metered AIS REST API (Vessels, PortCalls, ExpectedArrivals, MasterData, Distance, plus subscription feeds VesselsList and LiveData) with a separate Container Tracking API that returns shipment schedules and real-time vessel positions by container number. VesselFinder also runs a public web map, iOS/Android apps, an embeddable map widget, a fleet explorer, and a route planner.

providers.name: Maersk
providers.description: A.P. Moller - Maersk is the Danish integrated container shipping and logistics company. Maersk operates one of the world's largest ocean fleets and a global network of warehouses, inland transport, customs services, and air-freight capacity through Maersk Air Cargo. The Maersk Developer Portal exposes a catalogue of APIs for Track and Trace, Ocean Booking (DCSA-aligned), Schedules, Product Offers and pricing, electronic Bills of Lading, Verified Gross Mass, Demurrage and Detention, Air Booking, VGM, and container Maintenance and Repair. Many of Maersk's APIs implement Digital Container Shipping Association (DCSA) interface standards so the same client can address multiple carriers.

providers.name: SEDNA
providers.description: SEDNA is the operating system for shipping — a communications and workflow platform that unifies email, voyage and trade operations, and document handling for maritime, commodity trading and logistics teams. Its API (version 2019-01-01) exposes messages, contacts, teams, users, job references, category tags, events and workflows over a JSON:API-style REST interface secured with OAuth 2.0 client-credentials, letting developers automate inbox routing, tagging, subscriptions and third-party integrations. Backed by Insight Partners.

providers.name: Navis (Kaleris)
providers.description: Navis (now operated by Kaleris) provides terminal operating systems and supply chain software for the maritime and intermodal industries. The flagship N4 product offers APIs for container tracking, vessel planning, berth scheduling, yard management, and gate operations, serving 650+ organizations across 95+ countries.

providers.name: Evergreen Marine Corp.
providers.description: Evergreen Marine Corp. (Taiwan) Ltd. (TWSE: 2603) is a worldwide container shipping company founded by Dr. Yung-Fa Chang in 1968; since 2007 its group carriers have operated under the Evergreen Line brand. Through its ShipmentLink e-commerce platform it offers online cargo tracking, vessel schedules, booking, e-B/L, VGM submission, EDI services and an API Developer Portal with a catalogue of APIs such as shipment Track & Trace, available to customers after an application and registration process.

providers.name: MarineTraffic
providers.description: MarineTraffic is the leading maritime intelligence and AIS ship-tracking platform — now part of Kpler. The MarineTraffic AIS Data API exposes the same live + historical vessel positions, port calls, berth calls, vessel master data, voyage forecasts, predictive arrivals, port-congestion analytics, sea-lane routing, reverse geocoding, and fleet management endpoints that power the public marinetraffic.com map and the Kpler maritime data services. Data is sourced from 13,000+ terrestrial AIS receivers plus satellite AIS, served as REST/JSON (with CSV / XML / JSONO alternatives), authenticated via a per-key prepaid credit balance, and metered in credits per response row with per-service refresh-interval caching.

bands.label: Thin
bands.blurb: Limited machine-readable signal beyond documentation a human can read.

providers.name: Voyager Portal
providers.description: Voyager Portal is an AI-powered voyage and demurrage management platform for bulk commodity charterers, traders, brokers, and manufacturers, streamlining maritime shipping workflows from pre-fixture planning through post-fixture claim resolution. The platform provides AI-driven demurrage claims management and laytime calculations, cargo allocation, AIS vessel tracking, ETA tracking, noon reporting, and analytics, and exposes a documented public REST API for managing voyages, cargoes, claims, SOFs, vessels, ports, and workflows, plus outbound webhooks.

providers.name: HMM
providers.description: HMM Co., Ltd. is a South Korean shipping and logistics company headquartered at the Hyundai Group Building in Seoul. Its services include container shipping (general, reefer, oversized and dangerous cargo), bulk shipping (tankers, gas tankers, pure car and truck carriers, heavy lift and project cargo), terminals and intermodal transport. HMM says it launched four API services in 2022 and is adding more, from booking through to payment, that follow the Digital Container Shipping Association (DCSA) standards. The APIs are offered through the HMM Open API Developer Portal (apiportal.hmm21.com), where companies sign up and wait for approval before using them. The gallery lists APIs such as DCSA Arrival Notice, DCSA Booking and e-BL Company ID receipt.

providers.name: Port Community Systems
providers.description: Port Community Systems (PCS) are neutral and open electronic platforms enabling intelligent and secure exchange of information between public and private stakeholders to optimise, manage, and automate efficient port and logistics processes through a single submission of data.

providers.name: CargoSmart
providers.description: CargoSmart (now operating as IQAX) is a global shipment management software provider that gives shippers, consignees, freight forwarders, and logistics service providers ocean freight booking, container tracking, vessel scheduling, and shipping documentation tools across multiple ocean carriers. CargoSmart co-founded the Global Shipping Business Network (GSBN), a blockchain-based data exchange for carriers, terminals, banks, and customs authorities, and exposes its APIs so trading partners can embed booking, visibility, schedule, and documentation workflows directly into TMS, ERP, and supply-chain platforms.

providers.name: WaveBL
providers.description: WaveBL is an Israeli digital trade platform, headquartered in Kfar Saba and founded out of the ZIM shipping group, that moves original electronic bills of lading (eBLs) and the trade documents around them between carriers, freight forwarders, cargo owners, customs brokers and banks. Its blockchain-backed, peer-to-peer network issues, endorses, transfers, amends and surrenders title documents without a central repository, and is sold as the WaveBL Digital Document Hub, electronic Master and House Bills of Lading, WaveBL for Customs and a trade finance module that presents structured documents to banks. It is used by MSC, ZIM, Hapag-Lloyd, ONE, PIL, Evergreen and Leschaco among others, is approved by the International Group of P&I Clubs, and has implemented the DCSA Standard Annex for eBL Platform Interoperability so eBLs can cross to other platforms. WaveBL runs a real API programme — it states publicly that its platform complies with the DCSA OpenAPI specification for Issuance and the DCSA eBL Surrender Response API — but it operates no developer portal, publishes no API reference, base URL or machine-readable specification, and its only public API article lived on a Zendesk help centre that has since been decommissioned.

providers.name: Kpler
providers.description: Kpler is a commodities intelligence and maritime data platform that tracks cargoes, vessels, and trade flows across oil, refined products, LNG, LPG, and dry bulk markets. Kpler owns MarineTraffic and FleetMon (acquired 2023) and acquired Spire's maritime AIS business (2025), giving it one of the largest terrestrial and satellite AIS vessel tracking networks in the world. Its Direct Access REST APIs deliver trades, flows, vessels, port calls, freight metrics, and inventories per commodity platform, while MarineTraffic APIs deliver live vessel positions, port calls, voyages, and vessel particulars. API access is customer-gated behind an enterprise subscription, but the documentation, Python SDK, and endpoint surface are publicly published.

providers.name: Sinay
providers.description: Sinay is a maritime data and analytics company whose Developers Platform exposes a marketplace of REST APIs for the shipping and ocean-tech industry - vessel and port lookup from combined satellite and terrestrial AIS, metocean (weather and ocean) conditions, per-voyage CO2 emissions modeled on the GLEC Framework, ETA prediction, live port congestion, sailing schedules, and underwater noise. Every API is called over HTTPS at api.sinay.ai, authenticated with a single API_KEY header, and metered as monthly API units / credits with a free developer key to start.

providers.name: AISStream
providers.description: AISStream.io is a free service that streams global real-time AIS (Automatic Identification System) vessel-tracking data over a WebSocket. Clients register for a free API key, open a secure WebSocket to "wss://stream.aisstream.io/v0/stream", and send a JSON subscription message declaring one or more geographic bounding boxes plus optional MMSI and message-type filters. The server then pushes a continuous stream of AIS messages - PositionReport, ShipStaticData, and the full set of ITU-R M.1371 message types - each wrapped in an envelope carrying MessageType, MetaData, and the decoded Message. There is no REST API; the service is WebSocket-only.

providers.name: Saildrone
providers.description: Saildrone is an Alameda, California maritime autonomy company that designs, manufactures, and operates a global fleet of wind/solar-powered autonomous surface vehicles (USVs) for ocean science, maritime domain awareness, and defense applications. Founded in 2012 by Richard Jenkins, the company runs four USV classes — Explorer (23ft, environmental sensing), Voyager (33ft, MDA and counter-narcotics), Surveyor (65ft, deep-ocean bathymetric mapping), and the newer Spectre (ISR / anti-submarine warfare / kinetic payloads). Saildrone has logged over 2.5M nautical miles and 65,000 days at sea across customers including NOAA PMEL, NOAA SWFSC, the US Navy (Task Force 59), NASA, EUMETSAT, BOEM, and Lockheed Martin (which invested $50M in October 2025). Saildrone delivers data through two product surfaces — the Saildrone Mission Portal (secure web app for tasking and live multi-INT visualization) and the Saildrone Public Mission API (BETA) at developer-mission.saildrone.com, which exposes key/secret authenticated endpoints for health, drone access discovery, and time-series retrieval across vehicle, atmospheric, oceanographic, and biogeochemical datasets. Open ocean data from past missions is published via NOAA PMEL ERDDAP and NCEI under open-data terms.

providers.name: Searoutes
providers.description: Searoutes is a maritime routing and carbon-emissions API platform for logistics, freight forwarding, and supply-chain teams. Its REST APIs compute point-to-point, port-to-point, and port-to-port sea routes with distances and durations (including SECA, HRA, and ice-area avoidance), geocode ports, airports, and places, calculate multimodal CO2e emissions (sea, road, rail, air, inland waterway) using a GLEC-accredited methodology, track vessels via AIS (positions, ETAs, traces, arrivals), look up carriers and services, and return historical, real-time, and forecasted weather along routes. All APIs are served from https://api.searoutes.com and authenticated with an x-api-key header.

providers.name: Datalastic
providers.description: Datalastic is a maritime data API providing real-time AIS vessel tracking, historical ship movements, vessel specifications, and global port data over a simple REST interface. A database of 750,000+ ships is queryable by MMSI, IMO, or UUID for live position, speed, course, heading, destination, and ETA, plus zone traffic monitoring around any coordinate or port, up to 31 days of historical track per request, vessel and port finder search, and asynchronous bulk reports. Access is subscription-based with a monthly credit model and api-key authentication.

providers.name: Adopte Un Conteneur
providers.description: Adopte Un Conteneur is a French company that sells new and used maritime containers, modular bungalows, self‑storage boxes and accessories, delivering throughout France. Operating from 17 Rue de l'Isère, 31500 Toulouse under the legal name SAS BRYT DEVELOPPEMENT, it serves professionals, collectivités and private customers with a range of container sizes and options.

bands.label: Emerging
bands.blurb: More than an index entry but still mostly links rather than artifacts.

providers.name: AISHub
providers.description: AISHub is a cooperative AIS (Automatic Identification System) data sharing network for vessel tracking. Members who contribute a raw NMEA AIS feed from their own receiver (via UDP) get free access in return - a real-time aggregated feed from 1,500+ stations across 80 countries, plus an HTTP web service that returns vessel positions and station metadata as XML, JSON, or CSV. There is no pay-for-access tier; API credentials are earned by sharing a feed that meets coverage and uptime quality thresholds.

providers.name: AIS Trail
providers.description: AIS Trail provides a unified API delivering historical and real-time Automatic Identification System (AIS) data for vessels worldwide. The service offers clean, standardized, and query‑ready ship movement information, supporting use cases such as live tracking, route analysis, and maritime analytics. Users can access vessel positions, historical routes, and source metadata through a consistent RESTful interface, enabling integration into logistics, compliance, and marine research applications.

providers.name: MyShipTracking
providers.description: MyShipTracking is a real-time terrestrial AIS vessel-tracking platform. Its REST API delivers live vessel positions, voyage and static particulars, vessels within a geographic zone or near a reference ship, historical tracks, port details, port calls, estimated arrivals, and fleet management - all returned in a standardized JSON or XML envelope. Access is credit-metered under monthly subscription plans or a pay-per-use coin model, authenticated with an API key over Bearer or x-api-key.

providers.name: Kymeta
providers.description: Kymeta Corporation is a Redmond, Washington satellite communications company that builds electronically steered, flat-panel metamaterial antennas and the connectivity service that runs behind them. Spun out of Intellectual Ventures in 2012 from metamaterials research begun at Duke University, Kymeta ships the u8 terminal family — Osprey u8, Goshawk u8, Peregrine u8, Hawk u8 and the compact Kestrel u5 — for military and government, maritime, land-mobile, energy and humanitarian users who need multi-orbit GEO/LEO connectivity on the move. The hardware is paired with Kymeta Connect, a software-defined service platform reached through the Kymeta Access app and the Kymeta Access Portal, which handles terminal management, subscriptions, usage metrics and remote monitoring. Kymeta operates a first-party API host and its own OAuth 2.0 / OpenID Connect identity provider, but publishes no public developer program, API reference or machine-readable contract; product documentation and release notices require a Kymeta Access Portal account.

providers.name: Arundo Analytics
providers.description: Arundo Analytics is an industrial AI company with offices in Oslo, Stockholm, Heidelberg and Houston, building software for asset-heavy industries such as oil and gas, maritime and shipping, chemicals and manufacturing. Its Arundo AI Foundation platform combines a knowledge graph of asset hierarchies and sensor metadata, industrial time-series storage built for high-velocity sensor data, parallelised machine-learning model orchestration, and specialised AI agents, surfaced through the AI Foundation Studio and what the company calls the Arundo Foundation APIs. Packaged applications include Marathon (continuous equipment condition monitoring), ArundoEdge and Edge Manager (secure streaming of IoT sensor data from control systems to the cloud), Energy Optimizer, CarbonPath (Scope 3 emissions management for shipping) and AI Companion. Arundo also maintains the open-source Python packages ADTK (unsupervised time-series anomaly detection) and tsaug (time-series augmentation), and publishes a public Foundation compute plug-in contract on GitHub. The Foundation APIs themselves are marketed on the public site but are not publicly documented; there is no developer portal, no public API reference and no machine-readable specification, and the applications sit behind an Auth0 customer login.

providers.name: Aegis Marine Shipmanagement
providers.description: Aegis Marine Shipmanagement Inc. is a privately owned marine vessel transportation and ship management company headquartered at 215 South Road and King Street, Lacytown, Georgetown, Guyana, with a secondary office in Brooklyn, New York. Founded in 2018 by Guyanese-American businessman Sean Clarke, it serves the oil and gas sector, operating crude oil tankers, liquefied natural gas tankers and offshore support service vessels on behalf of third-party owners, partners and investors. Its services span commercial, technical, safety and quality, and logistics ship management, delivered through partnerships with established marine service providers, and include vessel registration under various flags, technical inspection and marine engine spares, marine vessel chartering, commodity trader engagement, and crew management covering recruitment, familiarization, training, retention and career promotion. Aegis Marine Shipmanagement is a shipping operator rather than a software vendor. It publishes no developer portal, no API documentation, no SDKs and no commercial or partner-facing product API. The only machine-readable interface it exposes is the WordPress core REST content API behind its corporate website at aegisships.com, which is captured here for discovery purposes: it is anonymously readable, effectively read-only, and serves the marketing site's own pages, media and taxonomy rather than any fleet, chartering or vessel-operations data.

providers.name: Pelyr
providers.description: Pelyr provides free maritime intelligence through an HTTPS AIS API, a live WebSocket stream, and a vessel map. The platform offers radar and satellite imagery, route change detection, zone alerts, and a developer portal with documentation, pricing, and support. It targets developers and businesses needing vessel position data for non‑commercial and commercial use.

providers.name: Marlo Technologies
providers.description: Marlo is a maritime ERP platform for dry bulk, tanker, and commercial shipping companies, unifying chartering, voyage management, finance, banking, and compliance in a single system. Operators use Marlo to plan charters, track voyage operations and cargo, model voyage P&L and cashflow, run valuations and credit scoring, manage loans and covenants, hold multi-currency accounts with FX transfers and corporate cards, and handle sanctions screening, emissions tracking, and CII rating management. Marlo is a Techstars-backed company and holds SOC 2 (AICPA) certification. It was surfaced as a portfolio company of Techstars and added to the API Evangelist network. As of this pass the company exposes a customer web application (app.marlo.co) but publishes no public developer API, API documentation, or SDKs.

providers.name: Sea Machines Robotics
providers.description: Sea Machines Robotics builds autonomous command-and-control systems (SM300-SP, SM300-NG) and computer-vision perception (AI-ris) for commercial and defense marine vessels. In September 2025 it announced the SMLink Streaming-API and SMLink Control-API, partner-gated interfaces that stream real-time vessel telemetry to external systems and let approved third parties command SM300 autonomy functions from their own mission software. These interfaces are embedded, vessel-side product features, not a self-service public developer platform; access is arranged through Sea Machines sales.

providers.name: Spire Maritime
providers.description: Spire Maritime (Spire Global) delivers satellite and terrestrial AIS vessel data - global ship positions, static vessel characteristics, voyage and destination data, port events, and predicted ETAs. The flagship Maritime 2.0 service is GraphQL-first at a single endpoint (https://api.spire.com/graphql, Bearer token auth), with a separate raw-TCP AIS stream for real-time message delivery in NMEA 0183 format. Access is enterprise / contact-sales. NOTE - following Spire Maritime's acquisition by Kpler, these APIs are being migrated/discontinued; new integrations are directed to developers.kpler.com.

providers.name: CMA CGM
providers.description: CMA CGM is a Marseille-headquartered French container shipping, logistics, and port operator and the third-largest ocean carrier in the world. Founded in 1978 by Jacques Saadé and led today by Chairman & CEO Rodolphe Saadé, the CMA CGM Group operates a fleet of 593 vessels with 4.5 million TEU of capacity calling 420 ports across 160 countries on 257 maritime services. The group includes maritime brands ANL, APL, CNC Line, Containerships, Comanav, and Mercosul Line; terminal operator CMA Terminals and Terminal Link; the CEVA Logistics contract logistics and freight forwarding business (acquired 2019); CMA CGM Air Cargo; Brittany Ferries and La Méridionale passenger ferries; and the CMA Média portfolio (La Provence, La Tribune, BFM-RMC, Brut). Through api-portal.cma-cgm.com the group exposes a DCSA-aligned REST API surface — Track and Trace v1 (DCSA v2.2.0), Schedules, Booking Request, Quotation, and Invoice — plus a parallel EDI catalog (EDIFACT IFTSAI, IFTMBF, IFTSTA, INVOIC) and group-level digital initiatives including ZEBOX (startup accelerator), Traxens-based IoT smart containers, and a strategic AI partnership with Mistral.

providers.name: Boatsetter
providers.description: Boatsetter is a Fort Lauderdale, Florida founded and Miami headquartered peer-to-peer boat rental marketplace that connects boat owners with renters and with United States Coast Guard licensed captains. Founded in 2012, the platform lists more than 50,000 boats across 600 to 700 locations worldwide and 20,000 makes and models, spanning fishing boats, pontoons, sailboats, party boats, watersports vessels and luxury yacht charters, bookable either bareboat or with a captain. Boatsetter layers identity verification, an insurance program underwritten through its Buoy partnership, payments, messaging, calendar and pricing tools for owners, and trust and safety on top of owner supplied inventory, and takes a marketplace commission on each booking. The company also operates a separate Boatsetter Owner application for hosts, and in December 2025 announced a merger with Getmyboat to form a combined boat rental marketplace expected to process roughly 500 million dollars in bookings across 50 countries, with both platforms and apps continuing to operate. Boatsetter does not publish a public developer API, OpenAPI definition, SDK, developer portal, or partner API documentation; its only public GitHub presence is a single archived fork of a jQuery form serialization plugin, and its third party surface is limited to consumer facing partnerships (Airbnb) and an affiliate marketing program.

providers.name: Kabal
providers.description: Kabal is the energy industry's leading logistics management SaaS platform. Founded in Norway in 2011 (formerly Wellit), Kabal provides an integrated, cloud-native platform that manages cargo, marine, transport, personnel, warehouse, rig and installation logistics across both offshore and onshore operations for oil & gas operators. The platform spans planning, execution and optimization, plus cost and emissions tracking and KPI reporting, connecting operators with their suppliers and vessels to share business-critical logistics data. Kabal is trusted by energy supermajors including ExxonMobil, Shell, Chevron, BP, TotalEnergies, Equinor, Petronas, Repsol, Eni and ADNOC, with tens of thousands of users across dozens of countries. Kabal received a growth investment from Insight Partners in 2023.

providers.name: Inmarsat
providers.description: Inmarsat is a British satellite communications operator founded in 1979, originally as the International Maritime Satellite Organization, providing voice, data, broadband, and IoT services over a global L-band, Ka-band, and multi-band fleet of geostationary satellites. In May 2023 Viasat completed its acquisition of Inmarsat, and the combined company now operates Inmarsat's GX (Global Xpress), BGAN, IsatData Pro (IDP), and Fleet Xpress services alongside Viasat's ViaSat-3 constellation as a unified multi-orbit network. Inmarsat serves four core markets — Maritime (NexusWave, Fleet Xpress, Fleet One, FleetBroadband, Inmarsat C/GMDSS), Aviation (SwiftBroadband, GX Aviation, Jet ConneX, SB-S safety services), Government (L-TAC, GX, BGAN M2M), and Enterprise/IoT (BGAN M2M, IsatData Pro, IsatM2M, NB-NTN). Inmarsat operates a developer program at developer.inmarsat.com with documented APIs for BGAN network management, GSPS voice, Global Xpress, IsatData Pro messaging, Fleet Edge assurance, and Fleet Edge hardware replacement; access to interactive Swagger documentation is gated behind developer registration and approval, though the IsatData Pro Messaging API has an open-source Apache-2.0 Node.js client published on GitHub. Inmarsat is also one of the participating operators in the GSMA NB-NTN (Non-Terrestrial Network) standards work for satellite-extended cellular IoT, with Viasat-led proof-of-concept code for NIDD (Non-IP Data Delivery) published under the inmarsat-enterprise GitHub organization.

providers.name: Harbor Lab
providers.description: Harbor Lab is an AI-powered port cost and disbursement account (DA) management platform for the maritime industry, headquartered in Athens, Greece. Its cloud software helps shipowners, ship managers, charterers, and port agents manage port calls, validate and approve disbursement accounts, benchmark and negotiate port service pricing across a marketplace of thousands of port service providers, and automate payment and settlement — improving operational efficiency, digitizing the process, and delivering cost transparency across port cost management. The company is backed by Speedinvest, VentureFriends, Atomico, and others. As of this profile Harbor Lab exposes a web dashboard product only; no public API, developer portal, or documentation surface was found.

bands.label: Minimal
bands.blurb: Index entry only; little beyond a description and a link.

providers.name: Seaboard
providers.description: Seaboard Corporation is a diversified global agribusiness and transportation holding company headquartered in Merriam, Kansas, operating through Seaboard Foods (pork production and processing), Seaboard Marine (containerized ocean cargo between the United States, the Caribbean, and Central and South America), Seaboard Overseas and Trading Group (grain merchandising and milling), Seaboard Energy (renewable diesel), Transcontinental Capital Corporation (electric power generation in the Dominican Republic), Mount Dora Farms, and a minority interest in Butterball. Seaboard publishes no public developer API or developer portal; its only documented machine-to-machine integration surface is the Seaboard Marine Electronic Data Interchange program, which publishes an ANSI ASC X12 and UN/EDIFACT transaction-set catalog and onboards trading partners through a request form.

providers.name: Blue Water Autonomy
providers.description: Blue Water Autonomy is a Boston-based defense technology company building autonomous warships for open-ocean operations, with the goal of revitalizing U.S. shipbuilding through scalable, reliable, uncrewed naval vessels. Founded in 2025 by Rylan Hamilton (ex-U.S. Navy officer and founder of 6 River Systems), Scott N. Miller (ocean engineer and early iRobot engineer), and Austin Gray (former Navy intelligence officer), the company unveiled its 190-foot Liberty Class autonomous ship platform for the U.S. Navy in February 2026. Backed by a $50M Series A led by GV, Blue Water Autonomy operates from offices in Boston MA, Washington DC, Morgan City LA, and San Diego CA. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; the company publishes no public API, developer portal, or SDK surface as of this enrichment pass.

providers.name: Amogy
providers.description: Amogy is an energy-technology company decarbonizing hard-to-electrify sectors by converting energy-dense ammonia into dispatchable, zero-carbon electricity. Its AMMDrive power systems crack ammonia into hydrogen and nitrogen and convert the hydrogen to power for data centers, industrial facilities, microgrids, and maritime vessels, and it develops proprietary low-temperature ammonia-cracking catalysts. Backed by DCVC and other investors, Amogy has demonstrated the world's first carbon-free ammonia-powered maritime vessel and partners with firms such as Samsung Heavy Industries and Mitsubishi. This is a company profile in the API Evangelist network; Amogy publishes no public developer API surface at this time, so this record captures its corporate identity and public web properties rather than API artifacts.

providers.name: Ocean Aero
providers.description: Ocean Aero is a Gulfport, Mississippi maritime robotics manufacturer that designs, builds and operates the Triton, an environmentally powered Autonomous Underwater and Surface Vehicle (AUSV) that can both sail on the surface and submerge to collect data above and below the waterline and relay it back to shore. The 14-foot platform harvests wind and solar energy, carries pre-packaged or custom payloads for defense, ocean research and offshore energy missions, and is managed through Ocean Aero's own proprietary mission-control GUI with fleet-wide waypoint and payload management. As of this profile Ocean Aero sells vehicles, payloads and mission services — it publishes no public developer program, no API reference and no machine-readable API contract.

providers.name: Spire Global
providers.description: Spire Global operates a constellation of more than 100 LEMUR nanosatellites collecting maritime AIS, aviation ADS-B, GNSS-RO weather profiles, and RF geolocation data, and offers Space Services for hosted payloads and managed satellite missions. Its data products are exposed as developer-friendly APIs: Spire Maritime 2.0 (now operated by Kpler) delivers vessel-tracking AIS through a GraphQL endpoint; Spire Aviation publishes REST APIs and real-time streams for flight metadata, live ADS-B tracking, historic positions, and event feeds; Spire Weather and Climate provides RESTful weather and ocean data APIs including 30 years of maritime weather history; and Spire Space Services exposes a developer portal for managed satellite operations. Spire's APIs are documented at product-specific subdomains and authenticated with API keys.

providers.name: HavocAI
providers.description: HavocAI (Havoc) is a Providence, Rhode Island-based defense technology company building all-domain collaborative autonomy software and autonomous surface vessels for the U.S. Navy, U.S. Army and allied militaries. Its software suite pairs Havoc OS, an edge autonomy operating system for heterogeneous platforms, with Havoc C2 for one-to-many operator control, Havoc Insights for real-time sensor and telemetry analytics, and Havoc Connect, a resilient peer-to-peer overlay network for degraded or GPS-denied environments. The company builds the Rampage, Seahound, Kiakoa and Atlas autonomous surface vessels and is partnered with Hanwha on 200-foot ASVs. Enrichment probing in July 2026 found no public developer API, OpenAPI or other machine-readable contract, no developer portal or documentation, no published SDKs or packages, no MCP server, and no A2A agent card - the platform is delivered under defense contract rather than as a self-serve developer product.

providers.name: Vake
providers.description: VAKE is a Norwegian maritime domain awareness company that detects, identifies, and tracks "dark vessels" from space. The VAKE platform fuses satellite imagery, AIS signals, and machine learning to reveal hidden vessel activity at sea for governments and industry. Its three products are Pathfinder, which reconstructs a vessel's past, present, and predicted movements and searches satellite imagery for vessels that go AIS-dark; Overwatch, which monitors an Area of Interest around ports, critical infrastructure, and economic zones to surface unreported activity such as illegal fishing, transshipments, and spoofing; and Clearview, a machine-learning service that identifies dark-vessel observations in multispectral satellite imagery against a global vessel-signature database spanning 2016 to today. The platform is delivered as a web application (studio.vake.ai) backed by a private API (api.nemme.io); onboarding is sales-led rather than self-serve.

providers.name: Vatn Systems
providers.description: Vatn Systems is a Bristol, Rhode Island defense technology company founded in 2023 that designs and manufactures low-cost, modular autonomous underwater vehicles (UUVs/AUVs) and the autonomy, navigation and acoustic-processing software that runs on them. Its product line spans the Skelmir S6 (6-inch, man-portable, swarm-capable) and Skelmir S12 (12.75-inch medium-class) vehicles, Eyra 5.1 and Eyra 8.0 passive hydrophone arrays, and four software systems - INStinct (maritime inertial navigation for GPS-denied operation), PARse (embedded acoustic signal processing on ARM), FUSE (multi-sensor tracking, distributed as a Docker image) and AEsir (TAK-native sensor fusion and mission planning). Mission planning is delivered through an ATAK/CivTAK/MilTAK/WinTAK plugin and Fathom, a browser-based mission planner and vehicle configurator. Vatn raised a $60M Series A in December 2025 (total funding $76.5M) and acquired Crewless Marine. It publishes no public developer portal, API reference or machine-readable contract; every integration surface is reached through a demo request or supplier form.

providers.name: REGENT Craft
providers.description: REGENT Craft Inc. is a Rhode Island maritime mobility manufacturer building the Seaglider, an all-electric wing-in-ground-effect (WIG) vessel that floats on its hull, hydrofoils, and then flies within a wingspan of the water's surface at up to 180 mph. The company builds the 12-passenger Viceroy, the larger Monarch, and the uncrewed Squire defense drone, and operates a defense product line for ISR, contested logistics and MEDEVAC missions. REGENT is a vehicle manufacturer rather than a software company: it publishes no developer program, no public API and no machine-readable API contract. It does serve a real, hand-authored llms.txt at its website root, which is the only machine-readable artifact on its public surface.

providers.name: Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace AS
providers.description: Kongsberg Defence & Aerospace develops technologies and solutions for the defence, security and surveillance markets. It provides systems that protect people and critical infrastructure, ranging from deep‑sea to space applications. The company combines military and civilian expertise to serve defence, research and commercial customers.

providers.name: Blueworldtechnologies
providers.description: Blue World Technologies develops and manufactures high‑temperature PEM methanol fuel cell components and systems for maritime, stationary and heavy‑duty transportation sectors. The company aims to provide green, efficient alternatives to combustion engines and diesel generators, focusing on renewable methanol solutions and advanced fuel cell platforms.

providers.name: Windward
providers.description: Windward is a Maritime AI company headquartered in London and Washington D.C. delivering mission-grade, multi-source maritime intelligence for defense agencies, law enforcement, customs, energy and commodity traders, marine insurers, shippers, and financial institutions. Founded by CEO Ami Daniel, Windward fuses AIS data, remote sensing (EO, SAR, RF GEOINT), proprietary behavioral analytics, and generative AI into a single Maritime AI platform covering vessel screening, ownership and entity resolution, sanctions exposure, deceptive shipping detection, ship-to-ship transfer analysis, IUU fishing detection, smuggling detection, container tracking, and maritime infrastructure protection. Windward exposes its intelligence through the API Insights Lab, a unified GraphQL API at developer.windward.ai providing programmatic access to vessel risk scores, Organization Defined Risk (ODR), ultimate beneficial ownership, early detection signals, tracked shipments, carriers, and detention & demurrage data, along with webhooks and workflow automation. The company has no public REST/OpenAPI surface, no public SDKs, and no public GitHub org — its API is GraphQL-only with managed onboarding and expert-led implementation support.

providers.name: DP World
providers.description: DP World is an Emirati global logistics company that specializes in port operations, maritime services, and supply chain solutions. It manages and operates marine and inland terminals across more than 40 countries and operates a portfolio of digital platforms - including the CARGOES suite (Flow, Runner, TOS+, PCS, Customs), Searates, and the Digital Freight Alliance - that expose APIs and integrations for shipment visibility, freight pricing, terminal operations, and trade workflows.

providers.name: Corvusenergy
providers.description: Corvus Energy, founded in 2009, provides zero‑emission energy storage solutions for the maritime industry. The company designs, manufactures and deploys battery systems that power hybrid and fully electric vessels, aiming to reduce diesel consumption and CO₂ emissions worldwide. With over 1,300 installations and more than 50% market share in maritime zero‑emission solutions, Corvus Energy serves a global customer base across shipping, offshore, and ferry sectors, delivering innovative, reliable and sustainable power.

providers.name: Seafair
providers.description: Seafair is an AI-native ERP platform for maritime operations, unifying crew management, HSQE and regulatory compliance, technical maintenance (planned maintenance systems and defect tracking), and accounting into a single system for shipping companies and ship managers. Its AI compliance engine performs document search and framework reviews (such as DryBMS and TMSA) and embeds AI assistance directly into operational workflows. Seafair markets itself as API-first with fast ERP integrations, but does not currently publish a public developer portal, API reference, SDKs, or OpenAPI definition. Seafair is a portfolio company of Speedinvest and is tracked in the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Saronic Technologies
providers.description: Saronic Technologies designs, manufactures, and deploys AI-enabled autonomous surface vessels (ASVs) for maritime security, domain awareness, reconnaissance, logistics, and payload delivery. The Austin-based company sells to the U.S. Navy, allied defense forces, and select commercial and government customers. Vessel models include Spyglass, Cutlass, Corsair, and Marauder, ranging from 6 to 150 feet. The Echelon software platform provides mission planning, high-fidelity simulation, fleet command-and-control, and open architecture for third-party payload integration (ISR sensors, EW, comms, weapons). Saronic does not publish a public, self-service developer API; integrations are arranged through partnership and are subject to U.S. export controls (ITAR/EAR).

providers.name: Captain's Eye
providers.description: Captain's Eye is a Haifa, Israel-based maritime AI company (founded 2020 by Uri Ben Dor and Doron Oizerovich, backed by Techstars) that delivers real-time video analytics software for maritime and industrial safety. Its SaaS platform connects to existing CCTV cameras, radar, and thermal sensors aboard merchant vessels, yachts, cruise ships, ports, and on-land petrochemical and energy sites, applying custom neural networks and commercial AI models to detect fires, smoke, leaks, sea pollution, missing protective gear, unauthorized access, and equipment failures. It provides real-time alerts, remote monitoring, incident documentation, and operational data collection, monitoring 5,000+ cameras and having detected 100,000+ events. Access is delivered through a private web application and mobile apps rather than a public developer API.

providers.name: Hapag-Lloyd
providers.description: A German multinational container shipping company and one of the world's largest liner shipping companies. Operates a fleet of over 250 vessels serving approximately 600 ports across 130 countries with a focus on quality and reliability. Provides a public API portal (api-portal.hlag.com) exposing container tracking, schedule, and booking APIs to customers, partners, and logistics platforms.

providers.name: MSC Mediterranean Shipping Company
providers.description: MSC (Mediterranean Shipping Company) is a privately-held, family-owned global container shipping and logistics group headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland, founded in 1970 by Gianluigi Aponte and now led by CEO Soren Toft under the Aponte-Diamant family. MSC is the world's largest container shipping line by fleet size and capacity, operating roughly 900 cargo vessels with a combined intake of about 7 million TEU and controlling more than a fifth of global container capacity as of late 2025. The carrier offers a portfolio of digital shipment-management products through its myMSC e-business platform — including Instant Quote for online rate generation, online booking, electronic Bill of Lading and Sea Waybill issuance via eDocs, container Track & Trace, and the myMSC mobile app — and exposes a Direct Integrations program for shippers, freight forwarders, and NVOCCs that combines REST APIs and EDI message exchange. The MSC Developer Portal (developerportal.msc.com), hosted on Microsoft Azure API Management, publishes documentation and EDI message implementation guides for products such as the DCSA-aligned Track & Trace API (v1.2 and v2.2), Booking, Booking Confirmation (X12 301 / EDIFACT IFTMIN), and Shipping Instructions, alongside ANSI X12 and EDIFACT IFTMIN / IFTMBC / COPRAR reference documents. MSC also runs direct-integration partnerships with INTTRA, Infor Nexus, and CargoSmart. API and EDI access is not self-service: prospective integrators must submit a Direct Integration request, and fees may apply.

providers.name: ZIM Integrated Shipping Services
providers.description: ZIM Integrated Shipping Services Ltd. (NYSE: ZIM) is a global container liner shipping company founded in 1945 and headquartered in Haifa, Israel. ZIM operates in more than 90 countries, serving over 30,000 customers across more than 300 ports worldwide with a differentiated global-niche strategy focused on agile fleet management and select trade lanes. The company is publicly traded on the New York Stock Exchange and, as of 2026, is the subject of a pending acquisition by Hapag-Lloyd at approximately $35.00 per share. ZIM's digital surface includes the myZIM customer area, ZIMonitor cargo visibility, an electronic Bill of Lading (eB/L) service, a Draft B/L tool, EDI integrations for booking and shipping instructions, a mobile application, and a developer API portal at api.zim.com hosted on Microsoft Azure API Management. Access to the ZIM API requires registering through ZIM API Support and obtaining a security token; rate limits are set per organization at registration. No public OpenAPI specification, SDKs, or GitHub organization are published, so ZIM is profiled here as a Tier-3 catalog entry pending spec disclosure or partner access.

providers.name: AliciaBots
providers.description: AliciaBots is a maritime robotics company, backed by Techstars, that builds autonomous robot teams for cleaning and inspecting ship hulls. Its flagship Roverclean robot operates independently to remove marine growth and monitor hull condition in real time without interrupting a vessel's voyage, using self-learning adaptive systems, precision cleaning, and remote monitoring and control to improve fuel efficiency and help operators meet IMO regulatory standards. AliciaBots does not currently publish a public API or developer program; this profile tracks the company as a network lead.

providers.name: Austal
providers.description: Austal is an Australian shipbuilder and defence prime contractor, founded in Henderson, Western Australia in 1988 and listed on the Australian Stock Exchange since December 1998. It designs, builds and sustains customised commercial and defence vessels, including ferries and naval ships, from shipyards in Western Australia, the United States, Vietnam and the Philippines, having delivered more than 350 vessels for 122 operators in 59 countries. It also offers vessel sustainment, training and consultancy, autonomy, advanced manufacturing and platform systems. Its public website publishes no developer API, documentation or developer portal.

providers.name: Corepowerholdingspteltd
providers.description: Corepowerholdingspteltd, operating as Core Power, is a UK‑based engineering company developing ship‑based nuclear energy systems to provide reliable, low‑carbon power for maritime and remote industrial applications. The firm designs, integrates and deploys modular reactors, propulsion technologies and supporting infrastructure, aiming to accelerate the energy transition for shipping, offshore platforms and coastal communities. With a focus on safety, regulatory compliance and scalable solutions, Core Power combines expertise in nuclear engineering, marine architecture and clean‑tech innovation to deliver power where it is needed most.

providers.name: PierSight Space
providers.description: PierSight Space is an India-based space technology company building a constellation of Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) and Automatic Identification System (AIS) satellites for persistent, all-weather maritime surveillance of the world's oceans. Founded by former ISRO engineer Gaurav Seth, PierSight delivers near-real-time ocean monitoring (targeting ~30-minute data latency and 100% ocean coverage) to detect illegal, unreported and unregulated (IUU) fishing, monitor oil spills, protect Exclusive Economic Zones, support maritime insurance risk assessment, and improve shipping operations. The company has raised roughly $8M from investors including Alpha Wave Ventures, Elevation Capital, and Techstars. As of this enrichment pass PierSight sells data solutions to enterprise and government clients and does not publish a public developer API, SDKs, or API documentation.

providers.name: Ocean Network Express
providers.description: Ocean Network Express (ONE) is a Singapore-headquartered global container liner shipping company formed in 2017 through the integration of the container shipping businesses of three Japanese carriers — Nippon Yusen Kaisha (NYK), Mitsui O.S.K. Lines (MOL), and Kawasaki Kisen Kaisha (K-Line) — with commercial operations launching on 1 April 2018. Operating under the magenta "ONE" brand and the Standard Carrier Alpha Code ONEY, the company runs a fleet exceeding 2,200,000 TEU across 165+ weekly service loops calling at 244+ ports worldwide, making it one of the largest ocean container carriers globally. ONE participates in THE Alliance vessel sharing agreement and offers reefer, dangerous goods, out-of-gauge, and project cargo services alongside standard dry container moves. Its customer-facing digital surface centers on the ONE eCommerce platform (ecomm.one-line.com), which provides cargo tracking, instant quotation via ONE QUOTE (powered by Descartes Kontainers), spot booking, shipping instructions, electronic bill of lading, ePayment, and demurrage/detention inquiry. A partner-facing developer portal exists at developers.one-line.com alongside EDI integration channels, but ONE does not publish a fully open, self-service OpenAPI specification, public SDK, or open-source code at either the github.com/ocean-network-express or github.com/OceanNetworkExpress organizations (both exist with zero public repositories). Tracking, booking, and schedule integrations are most commonly accessed by shippers and BCOs through third-party aggregators (Vizion, Portcast, JSONCargo, Terminal49, Tradlinx) or via DCSA-conformant carrier APIs delivered under commercial agreement.

providers.name: ThayerMahan
providers.description: ThayerMahan, Inc. is a U.S. maritime autonomy and ocean-intelligence company headquartered in Groton, Connecticut, founded in 2016 and led by former U.S. Navy Vice Admiral Michael Connor. It builds and operates uncrewed surface and subsurface sensing systems — Outpost, SeaPicket, SeaGuard (a non-kinetic counter-UUV defeat system) and the TransparenSea data platform — combining passive acoustic arrays, electronic sensors, edge processing, AI classification and human analysts to deliver persistent undersea surveillance, port and critical-infrastructure security, subsea infrastructure monitoring, passive acoustic marine-mammal monitoring and illegal-fishing (IUU) detection for defense, government and commercial offshore customers. ThayerMahan sells outcomes as a service rather than developer tooling: it publishes no developer portal, no API documentation and no machine-readable contract. The only public reference to programmatic access is on the TransparenSea page, which states that contact reports are delivered by application programming interface (API), voice report, or other means in near real-time — a customer-delivery integration negotiated per engagement, not a self-serve public API. Its GitHub organization holds two forks of third-party tools and no first-party libraries.

providers.name: AICE
providers.description: AICE is a defense-technology company building the next generation of underwater defense systems: autonomous swarms of modular marine drones that secure naval assets and coastal infrastructure against evolving underwater threats. Founded in 2026 by former NASA engineer Gregoire Chomette and European Robotics Champion Remi Bouteiller, the company is part of the Y Combinator Spring 2026 batch, is based in the San Francisco Bay Area with hardware manufactured in France, and applies swarm robotics and AI to surveillance, detection, and protection of critical subsea infrastructure. AICE currently ships hardware and does not publish a public API, SDK, or developer platform; this profile tracks the company for the API Evangelist network.

providers.name: Andrenam
providers.description: Andrenam is a defense technology company building an AI-powered maritime sensing network for undersea surveillance. It develops mass-manufacturable, low-cost buoy-based autonomous sonar systems that deploy from manned and unmanned vessels to detect, track, and identify real-time maritime traffic using cloud and edge AI, then dispatch resources to priority areas. Its product line spans deployment, AI-enhanced detection, and integration with naval command-and-control systems, targeting government and military maritime-domain-awareness customers. No public API, developer portal, or documentation surface is currently published.

providers.name: Italian Hydrographic Institute
providers.description: The Italian Hydrographic Institute (Istituto Idrografico della Marina Militare) is part of the Italian Navy, responsible for marine hydrography, oceanographic research, and supporting naval operations with nautical charts, tide predictions, and maritime safety data. It provides scientific and technical expertise in oceanography, hydrography, and related maritime domains, serving both military and civilian stakeholders.

providers.name: Orbital Insight
providers.description: Orbital Insight was a Palo Alto, California geospatial analytics company founded in 2013 by James Crawford (formerly Bell Labs, Google Books, and NASA's Mars rover program). The company applied computer vision and machine learning to satellite imagery, aerial photography, AIS vessel signals, and IoT/mobile location data to produce intelligence on supply chains, global commodities (notably oil storage via its Global Geospatial Crude Index), geopolitical events, demographics, retail foot traffic, disaster damage, and national-security questions. Its flagship product was the GO platform (later rebranded TerraScope), a self-service geospatial intelligence platform layering proprietary models over commercial satellite imagery from partners including DigitalGlobe, Airbus, Planet Labs, and e-GEOS. Orbital Insight raised funding from In-Q-Tel, GV (Google Ventures), Sequoia Capital, CME Ventures, and others, and acquired Boston-based FeatureX in 2018. After a period of financial distress in 2023, Orbital Insight was acquired by Privateer (co-founded by Apple's Steve Wozniak and Alex Fielding) on May 6, 2024. Following the acquisition, the standalone orbitalinsight.com brand was wound down and the TerraScope platform is now offered by Privateer alongside its Wayfinder space-domain-awareness data engine, fused into Privateer's "Elements" all-domain data platform. As of 2026 there is no public self-service Orbital Insight developer API, SDK, or open-source release; the orbitalinsight GitHub organization has only two archived repositories (a region-aggregation reference and a fork of tileserver-gl) and no current developer portal.

providers.name: Fleetzero
providers.description: Fleetzero is a Houston-based maritime technology company, founded in 2021 and led by U.S. Navy veterans and shipping-industry experts, building battery-electric energy and robotics systems to decarbonize ocean shipping at cost parity with fossil fuels. Its Leviathan modular marine energy storage system, 3.8 MWh marine battery containers, and 55 MWh battery barges provide propulsion power and mobile charging infrastructure for cargo vessels. Backed by Obvious Ventures, Fleetzero was added to the API Evangelist network as a portfolio-lead stub; it currently publishes no public developer, API, or documentation surface, so this profile carries company identity and infrastructure signals only.

providers.name: Iridium
providers.description: Iridium Communications Inc. (NASDAQ: IRDM) is a McLean, Virginia satellite communications company operating a constellation of 66 cross-linked Low Earth Orbit (LEO) satellites that deliver truly global L-band voice, data, IoT, and positioning/navigation/timing (PNT) services across every region of the Earth, including the polar oceans. Iridium sells satellite phones (Iridium Extreme), satellite messengers, satellite IoT modules and modems (Iridium 9602/9603, Iridium Certus 9770/9810/9704, Iridium Edge, Iridium Edge Pro, Iridium Edge Solar), Short Burst Data (SBD) messaging, broadband Certus terminals, and next-generation Iridium NTN Direct 5G Non-Terrestrial Network services built on 3GPP NB-IoT for direct-to-device smartphone and IoT connectivity. Iridium CloudConnect — co-developed with Amazon Web Services — pipes satellite IoT data as JSON into customer-owned Amazon SQS queues inside their own AWS VPC over a dedicated private Iridium-AWS interconnect, making Iridium the first global cloud-native satellite IoT backhaul. The company serves aviation, maritime, government/defense, land-mobile, autonomous systems, and IoT markets through a partner ecosystem of more than 500 service providers, value-added resellers, and hardware OEMs, and in May 2026 announced a planned acquisition of Aireon, operator of the world's only space-based air traffic surveillance network. Iridium's business model is airtime/subscription revenue plus hardware module licensing and engineering services; there is no public, self-service developer API or OpenAPI — network access is mediated through Iridium-authorized service providers, the Iridium CloudConnect AWS integration, and hardware-level AT-command and SBD interfaces on Iridium modems.

providers.name: Philly Shipyard
providers.description: Philly Shipyard (now Hanwha Philly Shipyard, Inc.) is a commercial shipbuilder based at the former Philadelphia Naval Shipyard, constructing Jones Act-compliant container ships, product and Aframax tankers, and National Security Multi-Mission Vessels (NSMVs) for the U.S. Maritime Administration and state maritime academies. In December 2024, Hanwha Systems and Hanwha Ocean (subsidiaries of South Korea's Hanwha Group) completed the acquisition of Philly Shipyard for approximately $100M, rebranding the operation as Hanwha Philly Shipyard Inc. (HPSI). No public developer APIs have been identified at this time.

providers.name: Carbon Ridge
providers.description: Carbon Ridge provides modular onboard carbon capture solutions for maritime shipping, enabling vessels to reduce CO₂ emissions directly at sea. Their technology integrates with existing ship systems to capture and store carbon, supporting the maritime industry's transition to net‑zero operations. The company focuses on scalable, retrofittable units that can be deployed across various ship classes, offering a practical path toward greener shipping and compliance with emerging environmental regulations.

providers.name: Dimeq
providers.description: Dimeq is a Norwegian maritime safety technology company working to prevent loss of life at sea and set new health, safety and environmental (HSE) standards for the maritime sector. Its Eye-D System is an IoT-based digital ecosystem that delivers real-time positioning of crew and passengers to one-meter accuracy during emergencies, man-overboard detection using environmental sensors, automatic mustering that registers people in seconds, and statistical analysis for accident documentation and prevention, while keeping data anonymous and GDPR-compliant outside of emergencies. The D-Router gateway supports Wi-Fi, Ethernet, PLC, fiber optics, UWB, Bluetooth, LoRa, ZigBee and MATTER connectivity. This is a hardware/IoT product company with no public developer portal, API, SDK or documentation surface at the time of enrichment.

providers.name: Seasats
providers.description: Seasats designs and manufactures autonomous uncrewed surface vehicles (USVs) for ocean intelligence, maritime domain awareness, and defense missions. Its platform lines include the hand-deployable Lightfish (6-month endurance), the fast-response Quickfish (35+ knots with an integrated drone bay), and the heavy-payload Heavyfish. Vessels carry modular payloads, run persistent autonomous surveys, and integrate with existing command-and-control (C2) architectures. Seasats is a Techstars-backed company. As of this enrichment pass Seasats publishes no public developer API, SDK, documentation portal, or machine-readable discovery surface; its integration story is C2 interoperability, not a web API.

providers.name: COSCO Shipping
providers.description: A Chinese state-owned multinational shipping and logistics conglomerate and the world's largest container shipping fleet by capacity. Operates container shipping, port terminals, bulk cargo services, and digital supply chain platforms (Syncon Hub, My Reefer, Hi-Dolphin) across global trade routes.

providers.name: Federal Maritime Commission
providers.description: The Federal Maritime Commission (FMC) is an independent agency of the United States government responsible for the regulation of international ocean transportation. The FMC oversees the practices of ocean common carriers, marine terminal operators, and other regulated entities.

providers.name: Chengrui
providers.description: Chengrui Power Technology (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. is a Chinese company specializing in port and maritime electrification solutions, energy storage, and smart shipboard power systems. The firm offers a range of products including shore power systems for ports, energy-saving and intelligent solutions for maritime operations, storage systems, and shipboard power equipment. Their mission is to become a leading domestic and world-class provider of new energy and electrical automation technologies for the maritime industry, delivering innovative, reliable, and efficient power solutions to support sustainable port and shipping operations.

providers.name: Arcboatcompany
providers.description: Arcboatcompany is a placeholder company currently lacking publicly available information about its services, products, or API offerings. This entry exists as a stub within the API Evangelist network, awaiting further discovery and verification of its digital presence, documentation, and operational details. The company’s official website, API endpoints, and related resources have not been identified at this time, and additional research is required to provide a comprehensive profile.

providers.name: Matson
providers.description: Profile for Matson in the API Evangelist network. Fortune F1000 (rank 947).
